result: Dense public CUDA Cast to/from E4M3FN/E5M2 uses shared ATen storage semantics with CPU; raw source storage chooses NaN sign because CUDA Half->F32 may canonicalize a negative signalling NaN.

private_math.correction: NaN narrowing sign now comes from original input storage bits, not arithmetic F32 widening; same helper on CPU/CUDA.

source.status: source prepared; no compilation, test execution or GPU operation performed
limits: CUDA Cast requires dense plain input/output with at least one FP8 port.
All transformations use original ATen kernels and managed temporaries; no external capture claim.

Initial CPU extraction was body-identical. Current raw-storage NaN-sign correction changes the shared body; CPU/CUDA runtime regression remains pending.

review.scope: Read-only independent source review of shared storage_cast, CPU call site and CUDA FP8 Cast admission/runtime/submit, plus narrow final raw-NaN-sign correction and corrected fixture identities. Only this scratch review report is updated; no product edits/build/tests/GPU execution by reviewer.
review.conclusion: No blocker found in the current frozen product source. The shared helper now intentionally corrects NaN narrowing sign using original input storage bits; it is no longer body-identical to the extracted old CPU function. Actual root CPU4/CUDA5 passes are recorded separately from this source-only review. Earlier fixture API/resource misses and the invalid arithmetic-sign assumption are explicitly corrected below.

cpu_extraction.comparison: Historical first extraction was independently compared byte-for-byte with the old CPU helper and was identical. Current shared header9f9859a5 intentionally differs: narrowing NaN sign comes from original storage bits instead of value.to(F32).signbit(). Do not apply the earlier body-identical conclusion to this final body. CPU call-site admission/dispatch remains unchanged.
cpu_extraction.scope: The helper is a private source header in hyle::compute::torch_shared. Only the original ATen CPU TU and original CUDA artifact TU include it. No public operation, API, macro, build option or backend dispatch registry was added.

storage_semantics.same_type: The helper returns input directly when source/target dtype match, then the CUDA submit path copies into the actual distinct caller destination. This avoids an FP8 -> F32 -> FP8 round trip that could alter NaN or storage codes.
storage_semantics.finite_fp8_saturation: The original ATen F32 value is clamped to +/-448 for E4M3FN and +/-57344 for E5M2 before the original conversion. E5M2 explicitly restores original infinities, while E4M3FN keeps its finite saturation. Thus finite overflow cannot accidentally use E5M2 infinity behavior, and this is ordinary storage Cast rather than scaled FP8 arithmetic.
storage_semantics.rounding: Numeric conversions retain the original locked ATen CPU/CUDA kernels. Existing c10 Float8 conversion definitions and the retained official Copy.cu expose nearest-even conversion; the CUDA E5M2 intrinsic path's no-saturation overflow is bounded by the helper's explicit clamp. No hand-written payload conversion loop was introduced.
storage_semantics.widening_nan_payload: For F32 destination, bitwise Tensor operations reconstruct original half/BF16/E5M2 NaN payloads and source sign. E4M3FN uses its signed canonical F32 NaN. This avoids relying on arithmetic conversion to preserve signaling payload bits. The final F32 result is a bit view of selected I32 values, not a numeric Int->Float conversion.
storage_semantics.narrowing_nan_sign: Final helper views original F32 as signed I32, original F16/BF16 as signed I16, and original FP8 as U8. I32/I16.lt(0) or U8&0x80.ne(0) determines source sign before numeric widening can canonicalize a negative signaling NaN. The existing value.flatten().isnan() mask still selects only NaNs; canonical low-target bits, finite clamp and original ATen rounding remain unchanged. This fixes the root-observed F16 0xfc01 negative-sNaN losing sign when narrowed into FP8 on CUDA.
storage_semantics.copy_contract: The retained pinned Copy.cu makes same-type, same-conjugation/sign, contiguous device copies memcpy-eligible. Both from_blob destinations and the helper's final views are dense same-dtype tensors. Therefore final copy_ does not intentionally round or canonicalize the helper's selected payload bits. Same-type FP8 also has an original typed identity-copy fallback.

admission_and_layout.domain: CUDA select requires one input/one output, plain dense descriptions, source and destination in F32/F16/BF16/E4M3FN/E5M2 and at least one FP8 endpoint. Nonfloating and unrelated non-FP8 Casts are declined, instead of falling through scalar()'s F32 default.
admission_and_layout.inference: Original output inference must exactly match the supplied destination description. The original temporary element-count bound rejects capacity above INT64_MAX/4, consistent with the largest F32/I32 element in this helper; aggregate live native temporary bytes remain unknown.
admission_and_layout.dense_proof: TensorDesc::is_dense for plain storage compares with the exact canonical dense descriptor, including byte strides. Thus submit's shape-only from_blob construction does not silently discard admitted noncanonical strides. Scalar and zero-sized descriptions are legitimate; empty Cast returns no_op before pointer wrapping or native kernels.
admission_and_layout.alias: Provider alias_support remains empty. Existing Compute validate_aliases checks actual resource/handle/range overlap before submit and rejects both same-address and partial source/destination aliases. Out-of-place destination writes and unchanged input are explicit test observations. No new private pointer or alias cache was added.

runtime_and_lifetime.cost: The Cast uses original kRuntime: shared Queue, managed replay, provider workspace, supports concurrent independent Invocations, conservative blocks_host=true and capture_compatible=false. Workspace/copy/repack/synchronization/dispatch and private-storage costs remain unknown rather than claiming zero or a fused single launch. RequireCapture must reject this path.
runtime_and_lifetime.queue_order: The actual Hyle QueueSequence stream is wrapped with getStreamFromExternal under the retained primary context and CUDAStreamGuard. All helper Tensor kernels and destination copy_ therefore use that actual ordered stream; there is no default-stream substitution or new host synchronization in submit.
runtime_and_lifetime.temporary_tensors: Intermediate ATen tensors are created/freed while the original external stream is current, preserving the original caching allocator's stream ownership. The final at::Tensor is kept in the existing per-Invocation result field. Dense same-type FP8 result may be the input from_blob view, whose external backing remains governed by the original Hyle binding/lease lifetime.
runtime_and_lifetime.accepted_prefix: Pointer/stream/context validation failures before ATen entry are rejected. Once dispatch starts, every exception is returned as accepted_command(failure()), so original QueueSequence finish and Completion retention remain responsible for any enqueued prefix. Provider invocation/program and Graph binding owners are retained through their existing Completion path; destroying temporary from_blob wrappers does not transfer external payload ownership.
runtime_and_lifetime.concurrency: Only immutable program metadata is shared. Native result Tensor state stays in independent Invocation objects; the original Compute/Graph admission prevents overwriting retained in-flight invocation state. This patch adds no shared mutable tensor scratch, new executor or extra completion policy.

tests_review.independent_reference: New tests reuse the existing independent storage-code oracle, including nearest-representable search and explicit IEEE NaN bits. They do not call the new helper as their expected-value function.
tests_review.numeric_scope: All256 FP8 codes widen to F32/F16/BF16; same-FP8 raw copies are checked; all65536 F16/BF16 patterns narrow into both FP8 types; cross-FP8 codes are covered. F32 midpoint neighbors, finite saturation, infinities, signed zero and signaling/quiet NaN bits are explicit.
tests_review.graph_scope: Public maximum/minimum/Cast/Cast Graph uses two owned slots, true GraphOutput leases, missing-output preparation failure/retry, actual input rebinding, retained old result and RequireCapture rejection followed by Commands. Direct admission tests cover noncanonical strides, exact overlap and empty/scalar cases.
tests_review.limits: The corrected fixtures have actual root-run CPU4 and CUDA5 passes, with zero skipped tests. This reviewer did not execute them. No new injected ATen allocation/dispatch exception or CUDA unknown-retirement fault test was added; these tests do not prove scaled GEMM, packed model coverage, capture performance or allocation-free inference.

review.freeze_metadata_correction: Final freeze corrects the existing AtenCpuCast count from3 to4; all5 product/test sources remain unchanged.

raw_sign_correction_review.legality: CPU and CUDA admission restrict storage_cast numeric arguments to exactly these five types. Each dtype view uses an equal-width integer type; no numeric reinterpretation or signed FP8 comparison occurs. Tensor.lt(0), bitwise_and, ne and where are ordinary ATen tensor operations.
raw_sign_correction_review.strides: The existing flatten before raw reinterpretation preserves logical element order. For noncontiguous or zero-stride CPU views, flatten produces/reuses a suitable contiguous 1-D logical tensor before equal-width dtype view; final view(input.sizes()) restores declared dimensions. CUDA still admits canonical dense tensors only. This change adds no dependence on original physical strides or storage offset.
raw_sign_correction_review.unchanged: Same-type early return, target-F32 payload restoration, finite saturation, E5 infinity restoration and numeric conversion code are unchanged. The new raw sign is consumed only by NaN canonicalization. No additional public API or macro.
raw_sign_correction_review.limits: Source reasoning is not exhaustive floating-point runtime proof; actual tests are root-run evidence below.

corrections_after_initial_review.fact: Actual test compilation rejected four GraphBuilder::add_node calls lacking explicit Operation wrappers. Initial static review missed the explicit-constructor API requirement. Exactly those four wrappers were corrected; product source was unchanged.

First runtime passed CPU4 and public Graph1; four Direct fixtures were rejected before math because descriptor-only prepare selected default system_resource. Initial review missed required actual GPU memory-resource arguments. Four calls now explicitly pass their real GPU resource; product source was unchanged.

After fixture corrections, real CUDA numeric execution exposed negative F16 signaling-NaN sign loss in arithmetic widening. The earlier review assumption that widened signbit preserves original NaN sign was wrong. Final product intentionally reads the original raw sign. This updates, rather than repeats, the initial body-identical and narrowing-sign conclusions.

root_actual_runtime.reviewer_action: Read final summary and source identities; did not compile or run tests/GPU.

test_review.scope: Narrow independent review of the5new FP8 Cast tests, their standalone storage oracle and exact frozen source identity. Product runtime/helper review remains with typed_gating_native; no build/GPU by this reviewer.

checks.fact: Each of256 FP8 source codes is checked against the preexisting non-ATen bit-format oracle when widening to F32/F16/BF16; same-format copy compares raw source bytes, including NaNs and signed zero. The Direct helper verifies selected Torch provider, unsupported alias, managed replay class and capture=false before submission.

F32 source corpus includes each adjacent finite FP8 midpoint and neighboring representable F32 values with both signs, finite overflow, both infinities and distinct signaling/quiet NaN signs. It uses independent raw-bit expected conversion, not Tensor::to as its oracle.

All65536 F16/BF16 storage codes and256 source FP8 codes exercise low-precision and cross-FP8 conversions. Expected() derives source F32 bits via the existing storage oracle and then target encoding; same-format identity remains raw bits.

Public Maximum/Minimum->FP8 Cast->F32 Cast Graph publishes both encoded and decoded outputs and checks2managed Cast steps. Two queues/invocations own independent inputs and WriteLease outputs. Captured replay is explicitly rejected, followed by Commands preparation before submission; no unsupported implicit capture is treated as success.

The loop retains actual GraphOutput from slot0 while slot1 resets/rebinds and executes its next round, then verifies slot0 prior payload. Before resetting slot0 it releases that retained GraphOutput. All temporary per-round GraphOutputs die at block end; reset while a real result remains is expected to fail. Source backing remains held until after fresh allocation, making nonidentical address verification meaningful.

Torch-only context isolates provider admission. Valid strided FP8 input is expected unsupported. Same-format exact input/output overlap is rejected without input mutation. Rank0 scalar and0-element shape are submitted independently; the empty path requires no fabricated pointer/math work and scalar signed zero is checked by storage oracle.

test_review.math_and_domain: Reviewed tests are for dense public FP8 storage Cast, not scaled/block FP8 quantization, model accuracy or a captured native FP8 kernel claim. Their managed/uncaptured assertions agree with temporary-allocating ATen carrier intent.
test_review.fixture_caution: Original source-review API no-blocker statement was wrong for explicit Graph Operation wrapping and Direct GPU resource arguments. Both failures and exact original review remain preserved; corrected calls were read against actual APIs.
test_review.test_wiring: fp8_cast_test.cc is added to the existing CUDA graph-route test target and its body is gated by HYLE_COMPUTE_TORCH_CUDA; no added test executable, SDK or validation matrix.
test_review.actual_results_claimed: Root-owned tests-complete actual CPU4/CUDA5, zero skips, read only by this reviewer; no reviewer execution
test_review.metadata_update: Final raw-source NaN-sign product correction changes shared helper, while final test and independent oracle are unchanged. No test assertion or coverage was weakened.

contract: RNE and finite FP8 saturation; E5 preserves true infinity; declared F32 widening NaN payload and narrow NaN sign; same-type out-of-place copies preserve storage codes. Empty operations are no-ops; scalar works. Public range/alias validation stays in the existing core.
execution: Existing original ATen CUDA kernels and Invocation result lifetime, managed and not capture-compatible, with unknown provider-private workspace. Non-dense storage is declined. No new public operation, executor, native kernel, SDK or model-name switch.
